#TheHungerGames

From acclaimed director Francis Lawrence, THE HUNGER GAMES: SUNRISE ON THE REAPING follows sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) from District 12, beginning on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Annual Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, the biggest Games yet with twice as many tributes. 

Set in the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, the story follows Haymitch into the arena, where he forms an unlikely alliance with fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) and joins a coalition determined to challenge the Capitol’s control under President Snow (Ralph Fiennes). As the competition unfolds, Haymitch risks everything to take down the Games from within the arena — setting in motion the rebellion that will change Panem forever.

Based on Suzanne Collins’ best-selling novel, THE HUNGER GAMES: SUNRISE ON THE REAPING also stars Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Maya Hawke, Whitney Peak, and Kelvin Harrison Jr. Produced by Nina Jacobson, Brad Simpson and Francis Lawrence. Screenplay by Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie.

snippet.title: POURQUOI J'ÉCRIS - Roxane Bruneau | Vidéoclip officiel
snippet.description:
Voilà, c’est officiel, cette vidéo marque officiellement le début de ma crise de la quarantaine même si j’ai pas quarante ans! On a eu envie de retourner dans le temps, de créer un clip comme ceux que j’écoutais à MusiquePlus quand j’étais kid! C’est juste qu’après 10 h à courir non-stop, faire des cascades pis du BMX, j’me suis rendue compte que j’ai vraiment passé l’âge! J’espère que le clip vous plaira, même si le vidéoclip est mort en général. C’est un format que j’aime tellement, on dirait que j’ai de la difficulté à lui dire au revoir 😭❤️

LES BRUNO’Z, j’ai hâte de lire vos commentaires !!

snippet.title: Other Mommy | Official Trailer 2
snippet.description:
There’s nothing like a mother’s love. Get tickets now. Other Mommy only in theaters October 9.

Can I go inside your heart?

From James Wan, one of the most influential architects of modern horror behind the Saw, Insidious and The Conjuring franchises—and Rob Savage, the director of bold genre films Host and The Boogeyman, comes a terrifying trip into the darkening world of a young girl, Bela, who forms a relationship with a sinister entity in her home who looks uncannily like her own mother.

Academy Award® winner Jessica Chastain (It Chapter Two, The Eyes of Tammy Faye) stars in a dual role as Bela’s mother and as “Other Mommy,” a manifestation of the entity. Jay Duplass (Transparent, Industry) plays Daddo, Bela’s father, and Arabella Olivia Clark (The Housemaid, The Hand that Rocks the Cradle) plays Bela. 

The impressive supporting cast includes Actor Award nominee Dichen Lachman (Severance), Emmy and Tony Award nominee Arian Moayed (Succession) and screen legend Karen Allen (Indiana Jones films).  

From Blumhouse Atomic Monster, Other Mommy is directed by Rob Savage from a screenplay by WGA award winner Nathan Elston, writer for the Emmy-winning sensation Succession, based on the New York Times bestselling novel Incidents Around the House by Josh Malerman (Bird Box).

The film is produced by James Wan, p.g.a., and is executive produced by Michael Clear, Judson Scott, Rob Savage, Josh Malerman and Ryan Lewis.

snippet.title: Proving Their "Impossible" Studio Sound Was Real | Boston "Foreplay / Longtime" Live 1979
snippet.description:
Boston - "Foreplay / Long Time" (Live at Giants Stadium, East Rutherford, NJ 1979)

Experience 1970s arena rock at its absolute, high-voltage peak! Welcome to the official live music archives, presenting a restored, high-definition concert recording of Boston performing their colossal two-part anthem, "Foreplay / Long Time."

Recorded live on June 17, 1979, at Giants Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, this pristine archival release captures the band headlining to a sold-out crowd of over 70,000 roaring fans. Touring behind their sophomore album *Don't Look Back*, the band reached back to their historic 1976 debut to deliver this blistering showcase of classical-inspired keyboards, soaring vocal harmonies, and twin-guitar firepower.

🚀 The Live Lineup:

🎤🎸 *Brad Delp* – Lead Vocals, Acoustic Guitar
🎸🎹 *Tom Scholz* – Lead & Rhythm Guitar, Hammond Organ, Keyboards
🎸🎤 *Barry Goudreau* – Lead & Rhythm Guitar, Backing Vocals
🎸🎤 *Fran Sheehan* – Bass Guitar, Backing Vocals
🥁 *Sib Hashian* – Drums, Percussion

📋 5 Fast Facts About the Performance & Liner Notes:

• *Tom Scholz's First Masterpiece* – The instrumental "Foreplay" was actually the first piece of music MIT graduate Tom Scholz ever wrote back in 1969. It was later seamlessly merged with "Long Time" for Boston's monumental debut album.
• *The Hammond Organ Intro* – Scholz recorded the complex, sweeping arpeggios of "Foreplay" on a Hammond M3 organ, creating one of the most recognizable, progressive-leaning instrumental intros in classic rock history.
• *Brad Delp's Vocal Acrobatics* – Often regarded as one of rock's greatest tenors, Brad Delp's ability to effortlessly transition from smooth, mid-range verses to stratospheric high notes live on stage is on full display during "Long Time."
• *The Giants Stadium Peak* – Headlining this massive summer festival event in New Jersey represented the absolute pinnacle of Boston's live stadium draw, translating their dense, multi-layered studio sound flawlessly to an outdoor arena.
• *Soundboard Master Audio Restoration* – Sourced directly from original multi-track soundboard broadcast tapes in the venue archives, this audio restoration balances the heavy keyboard layers, soaring dual-guitar leads, and Sib Hashian’s driving drum beat.

🔔 Subscribe to The Mosh Pit channel: https://bit.ly/4ufAmcS

Boston defined the sound of late 1970s rock, establishing a blueprint for radio-friendly, high-fidelity production that dominated global airwaves. Formed in 1976 in Boston, Massachusetts, the group featured Tom Scholz (guitar/keyboards), Brad Delp (vocals), Barry Goudreau (guitar), Fran Sheehan (bass), and Sib Hashian (drums). Their self-titled debut album remains one of the fastest-selling records in history, eventually achieving Diamond certification and moving over 17 million units in the United States alone.

The band utilized multi-tracked, layered guitar harmonies and precise, melodic arrangements that moved away from the blues-based improvisation common in the era. This technical approach helped codify the arena rock genre, influencing a generation of stadium acts through meticulously crafted compositions. Beyond their debut, the group secured massive commercial success with multi-platinum follow-ups like *Don't Look Back* and *Third Stage*, solidifying their position as architects of the polished rock sound.

snippet.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Review
snippet.description:
Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave reviewed by Brendan Graeber on Nintendo Switch 2.

"Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave builds upon its strategic arts in ways I couldn’t have anticipated. It’s never satisfied to make me grow only as a battlefield tactician, or only in my ability to manage my time between skirmishes wisely, but both in perfect harmony. Every time I turned around, I was being given more challenges to face and more tools to master in order to overcome them. The many unique twists of each hero’s story path had me eager to see all the ways those journeys differed from each other, making the grand culmination in the final act hit so damn well. Planning out my expeditions across an imposing map became an unexpected highlight that not only hooked me, but rewarded my persistence by continuing to expand all the ways I could direct my armies as I tried to stay on top of newly emerging threats. The scope of both its formidably challenging battles and intricate management systems would be wildly ambitious for one path, let alone spread across four – yet somehow Fortune’s Weave only gets better and better each time you guide its captivating heroes into the colosseum and far beyond."
